{
  "candidate_id": "v710-v710b-regression-on-q1-run-v79q1-accountancy-v5",
  "content_hash": "db6d88a5bca512288f3ecbc4edbf1734b39837caefeca4db258319d96284a776",
  "solved_key": "B",
  "single_defensible_answer": true,
  "source_support": true,
  "numeric_solution": false,
  "boundary_cases": true,
  "passage_integrity": true,
  "passage_answerability": true,
  "meaningfully_distinct": true,
  "evidence_ids": ["E1.1", "E1.2"],
  "reasons": [
    "Option B is verbatim supported by NCERT Class 12 Accountancy text on the fixed capital method, which specifies that capital accounts always show a credit balance remaining unchanged unless additional capital is introduced or capital is withdrawn by agreement.",
    "Option A describes the fluctuating capital method; under the fixed capital method, adjustments for profit share, interest, and drawings are entered in current accounts.",
    "Option C is contradicted because current accounts can have either a debit or a credit balance.",
    "Option D is contradicted because a partner's current account with a debit balance is shown on the assets side of the balance sheet."
  ],
  "syllabus_chapter": "Partnership Fundamentals",
  "syllabus_topic": "Fixed v/s Fluctuating capital",
  "syllabus_entitlement": true,
  "presentation_ready": true,
  "question_type_match": true,
  "principle_applicability": "excerpt_required",
  "decisive_principle_in_excerpts": true,
  "answer_conditions": [
    {
      "condition": "Partners' capital accounts are maintained under the fixed capital method.",
      "status": "explicit",
      "alters_key_if_changed": true,
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "option_challenges": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "strongest_reading": "Capital accounts record yearly adjustments such as profit, drawings, and interest under the fluctuating capital method.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "strongest_reading": "Current accounts can only have a credit balance and thus appear strictly on the liabilities side.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "strongest_reading": "Debit balances of partner current accounts are placed on the liabilities side as negative items.",
      "correct_under_reading": false,
      "reading_status": "contradicts_stem",
      "convention_evidence_ids": []
    }
  ],
  "blocking_defects": [],
  "style_notes": [],
  "cuet_fit": {
    "criteria": {
      "syllabus_objective": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Directly assesses Fixed v/s Fluctuating capital accounts under Partnership Fundamentals."
      },
      "format_authenticity": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Standard single-statement selection MCQ typical of CUET UG Accountancy."
      },
      "level_calibration": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Tests textbook conceptual definition of fixed capital method directly aligned with standard recall questions."
      },
      "discrimination_value": {
        "level": 3,
        "evidence": "Distractors effectively test confusion between fixed capital, fluctuating capital, and balance sheet presentation of current accounts."
      }
    },
    "reasoning_steps": 1,
    "estimated_difficulty": "easy",
    "cognitive_level": "recall",
    "exemplar_ids_compared": []
  },
  "option_resolution": [
    {
      "option": "A",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "Capital accounts change every year as profit share, interest and drawings are recorded in them",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "All items like share of profit or loss, interest on capital, drawings, interest on drawings, etc. are recorded in a separate accounts, called Partner’s Current Account.",
      "reason": "These adjustments are recorded in current accounts, not capital accounts, under the fixed method."
    },
    {
      "option": "B",
      "status": "supported",
      "false_part": "",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The partners’ capital accounts will always show a credit balance, which shall remain the same (fixed) year after year unless there is any addition or withdrawal of capital.",
      "reason": "Accurately restates the fundamental feature of the fixed capital method."
    },
    {
      "option": "C",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "always show a credit balance and appear only on the liabilities side",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.1",
      "premise_quote": "The partners’ current account on the other hand, may show a debit or a credit balance.",
      "reason": "Current accounts can have either a debit balance or a credit balance."
    },
    {
      "option": "D",
      "status": "contradicted",
      "false_part": "shown on the liabilities side of the balance sheet",
      "premise_source": "excerpt",
      "evidence_id": "E1.2",
      "premise_quote": "and on the assets side, if they have debit balance.",
      "reason": "A current account debit balance appears on the assets side, not liabilities."
    }
  ]
}
